component.name: PageLayout
component.description: Top-level page shell with structural variants (stack, two-column, full). Wraps content in a PageContainer to enforce max-width consistency and shares its size with descendant components (notably Header) via context so the full-bleed Header chrome and the constrained page body agree on width without prop-drilling.

useCases: Vertically stacked pages — most app screens (settings, lists, detail views without sidebars)
Two-column pages with a primary content area and a secondary aside (filters, summaries, related content)
Full-bleed pages where content needs the entire viewport (canvas, builders, full-screen data tables)

commonPatterns.name: stack-default
commonPatterns.description: Header full-bleed above; Body slot constrains the page content to the configured size

commonPatterns.name: two-column-2-1
commonPatterns.description: Main + aside at 2:1, aside on the right

commonPatterns.name: two-column-aside-left
commonPatterns.description: Aside on the left (e.g. table-of-contents, navigation list)

antiPatterns.reason: PageLayout is the page-level shell. Nesting creates double constraints and conflicting context.
antiPatterns.alternative: Use Stack for vertical rhythm inside; use PageLayout.Main + PageLayout.Aside slots for column splits.

antiPatterns.scenario: Using PageLayout inside a SidePanel.content slot
antiPatterns.reason: SidePanel is a constrained surface; PageLayout will compound the constraint and shrink content unpredictably. See governance LC-001.
antiPatterns.alternative: Use Stack for vertical rhythm inside SidePanel content.

antiPatterns.scenario: Wrapping app-shell chrome (Sidebar nav, SidePanel) inside PageLayout
antiPatterns.reason: PageLayout is page-level — only the main content area. Sidebar and SidePanel live in the app shell layout, alongside the page slot.
antiPatterns.alternative: Render Sidebar and SidePanelContainer in the app's root layout; render PageLayout inside the page slot.

antiPatterns.scenario: Hand-rolling a centered max-w-* div instead of PageLayout
antiPatterns.reason: Bypasses the shared size context, so Header won't agree on inner width and pages drift apart.
antiPatterns.alternative: Use PageLayout — it handles container width and propagates size to Header automatically.

semanticMeaning.stack: Vertically stacked sections — the default for most pages
semanticMeaning.two-column: Main content with a secondary aside (responsive — stacks on narrow viewports)
semanticMeaning.full: No max-width constraint — for canvas-style or full-bleed pages

slots.PageLayout.Body: Constrained body slot for stack variant — wraps children in a PageContainer at the layout's size
slots.PageLayout.Main: Primary content column in two-column variant
slots.PageLayout.Aside: Secondary content column in two-column variant — sits on the right by default

parentConstraints: Must not be nested inside another PageLayout
Must not be used inside a SidePanel.content slot

responsive.mobile: Two-column variant collapses to a single column (flex-col) below md breakpoint. asideSide is ignored on mobile — main always renders first.
responsive.desktop: Two-column uses flex-grow ratios (basis-0 grow-{n}) for true fluid columns; max-width is enforced by the surrounding PageContainer.

accessibility.role: Generic container — Aside slot uses the <aside> element for landmark semantics
accessibility.screenReader: Aside is announced as a complementary landmark; main content is in source order before aside regardless of visual side

rules: Default variant is stack — fits most pages
Header lives at the top of children, full-bleed; PageLayout.Body / .Main / .Aside slots are the constrained content surfaces
Stack variant: wrap body content in PageLayout.Body so it picks up the layout's size automatically
two-column uses flex-grow ratios (1:1, 2:1, 3:1) — never fixed pixel widths, so columns scale fluidly with viewport
Main is conceptually always the larger column; use asideSide to flip the visual order without inverting the ratio
Two-column collapses to a single column below the md breakpoint — content stacks vertically with the configured gap
Default size is lg (max-w-7xl, 1280px) — overrides at the PageLayout level propagate to Header automatically
Use variant=full for canvas pages; pair with Header contentSize=full so the Header inner content also bleeds
Do not pair the two-column variant with a centered max-width container inside Main or Aside — the columns are already constrained by the outer PageLayout

aiHints.context: PageLayout is the top-level page shell. Pick variant by structural intent: stack for vertically composed pages (the default), two-column for main+aside layouts (use flex-grow ratios, not fixed widths), full for canvas-style pages with no max-width. PageLayout shares its size with Header via context so the full-bleed chrome and the constrained body align on width without manual prop-drilling. Do NOT use PageLayout inside SidePanel content (LC-001) or nest it inside another PageLayout. App-shell chrome (Sidebar, SidePanel) sits alongside PageLayout, never inside it.
